steps.text: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring water to a boil, then immediately remove from the heat. Cover and let eggs stand in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes. Transfer eggs to a bowl of cold water; peel when cool.
Meanwhile, combine onion, balsamic vinegar, water, garlic, and sugar in a saucepan over high heat; bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and cool to room temperature, 30 to 45 minutes.
Place peeled eggs in a glass jar and pour cooled vinegar mixture over top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 to 5 days before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic-Pickled Eggs
raw_recipe.description: These balsamic vinegar-pickled eggs are flavored with onion and garlic. The dark brown color is sure to be a conversation starter at the table!
raw_recipe.name: Balsamic-Pickled Eggs

review.reviewBody: I really enjoyed this recipe. I was looking for a different pickled egg recipe and this was it. I was surprised by the strong garlic after taste. I think the quality of balsamic vinegar makes a difference in the overall taste. I will definitely make this again.

Very good...boiled the eggs a little longer and added 2 tbsp kikkoman soy sauce and a little cayenne after reducing the sugar by 1/2 in the brine. A nice change from the traditional pickled egg. My kids who usually only eat the yolks of hardboiled eggs and think traditional pickled eggs are too vinegary now enjoy eating the whites too thanks to the balsamic in this recipe

I heard a tip on the radio recently to use a cheap Sauvignon Blanc instead of vinegar in the jars. Looks better. Also instead of peeling them before soaking them in vinegar, crack the egg shell all over, soak in the vinegar, then peel.... a cool crackle appearance on the eggs!

This is one of my favorite recipes. When I make these I leave out the sugar. The balsamic vinegar can come off very strong for some people. Everyone that I have shared these with has gone back for more.

I loved the flavor of these eggs! I think the key is you have to really like balsamic vinegar. These eggs do not taste like traditional pickled eggs. The egg prep really depends on the eggs you use.... We use nest fresh eggs and the trick is to place eggs in cold water with1/8 cup salt per qt. Of water.... Bring to full boil...remove from heat... Cover and let set for 17 minutes....place eggs in to ice cold water until chilled. This way the eggs are cooked through and pop right out of the shell. Yummy thank for sharing the recipe!

I think the completely brown-colored egg is a bit overpowering (visually)for an otherwise nice way to make pickled hard-boiled eggs. A thought: Keep the shell on, but crackle the shell, then place the [shell-on egg] into the liquid. Leave it for a day, or maybe two, then peel it. You should have a wonderfully marble-effect egg.
This is our favorite pickled egg recipe. Just sweet enough and different than your standard pickled egg. We don't use the onion, just a preference, and they come out great.

These pickled eggs are not bad but not quite what I was looking for. My son loves pickled eggs but he did not like the little sweetness in these, I would probable leave the sugar out. The color is also very intimidating; if you can get past that it’s not a bad egg.
Very simple and straight-forward recipe. I will be bringing a jar of these for a Christmas party :)
Followed recipe as printed. These are our favorite pickled eggs. I made these because of the odd color and have made them 3 more times.
Quick and easy and a bit hit!
I loved it. Only change was replaced sugar with Stevia.
I was never a fan of pickled eggs until I made these. Just love the flavor.
These were awful. Unfortunately I'm not experienced enough to know what changes would have helped in this situation.

I made these right before Christmas so they would be ready for Christmas Eve get together. I really love balsamic so I knew these would be wonderful. I gave them five days in the fridge altho next time I'll make a huge batch so I can let them sit longer. The colour of these eggs is a rich brown. Another interesting thing was that when I placed them in a regular sized mason jar they ended up touching the sides and one another, resulting in these interesting white circles on them...looked great on the serving tray...some people didn't even know what they were :) I only crushed my garlic with the side of a knife but I think next time I'll microplane it for more garlicky flavour. Awesome awesome epic eggs!

We make Balsamic Pickled Eggs also and all we do boil the eggs, put them in a mason jar, pour Italian balsamic vinegar over them and let sit in the frig for a minimum of 3 days. Out of this world goooooood :)

honestly i loved the flavor! It's the egg preping that did not work. These eggs were only half cooked. I advise to fully boil the egg before aging. I questioned it before I made them, but wanted to follow the recipe exactly. If you like a sunny side up pickled egg..more power to ya! 3stars for flavor!!!!
